annotation.title_clean: Durkheim's Theory of the Division of Labor and Its Relevance for Socially Responsible Robotics
annotation.title_en: Durkheim's Theory of the Division of Labor and Its Relevance for Socially Responsible Robotics
annotation.venue: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications, Vol. 366 (Robophilosophy 2022), IOS Press
annotation.summary_en: Robophilosophy 2022 conference paper applying Durkheim's theory of the division of labor to robotics. It uses his three social pathologies (forced division of labor, excessive division of labor, anomie) to analyze the social and ethical impacts of workplace robots and sketches a socially responsible innovation approach.
key_provisions_or_claims: Durkheim's theory of division of labor and social solidarity is applicable to robotics innovation.
Forced division of labor, excessive division of labor and anomie form a framework for analyzing workplace robot impacts.
Robots can contribute to these social pathologies.
Proposes a form of socially responsible innovation informed by Durkheim.
